newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money dealers say small rise only temporary.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money dealers say small rise only temporary.

text.p: Dutch money market rates advanced a touch on Monday, but dealers said the slight rise was only temporary and rates would come off again.

"The rise might have been linked with dollar arbitrage as the dollar was quite a bit stronger today," said one dealer, adding that the rise was unlikely to continue. "Rates will slip a few basis points in the near-term," he said.
Call money rates were stable, but deposits added a couple of basis points. Three-month deposits rose two basis points to 3.02 percent bid.
Most business was done in the shorter-end, with the focus on call and deposits up to three months.
The guilder gained slightly against the mark at 112.240 per 100 marks versus 112.255 on Friday.
